kernels.definition: Electrical resistance describes how strongly a material or device opposes current; Ohm's law relates voltage, current, and resistance for ohmic conductors.

definitionAnchor.quote: The current that flows through most substances is directly proportional to the voltage V applied to it

facts.text: For an ohmic device at fixed temperature, current is proportional to voltage.

anchor.quote: current is proportional to the voltage

facts.text: Resistance depends on material, length, cross-sectional area, and temperature.

anchor.quote: resistance depends on the geometry and material

kernels.definition: A DC circuit is a conducting path with steady current, sources, and components whose voltages and currents obey conservation rules.

facts.text: Series components share the same current; parallel branches share the same voltage.
Kirchhoff's junction rule expresses charge conservation, and the loop rule expresses energy conservation.

kernels.definition: A magnetic field describes magnetic influence in space and determines magnetic forces on moving charges and currents.

facts.text: Magnetic field lines form closed loops and do not begin or end on isolated magnetic charges.

kernels.definition: Magnetic force on a moving charge depends on charge, velocity, magnetic field, and the angle between velocity and field.

definitionAnchor.quote: force on a moving charge in a magnetic field

facts.text: The magnetic force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the magnetic field.

anchor.quote: perpendicular to the velocity and magnetic field

facts.text: A charge moving parallel to a magnetic field experiences no magnetic force.

anchor.quote: zero when velocity is parallel to the field

kernels.definition: Faraday's law states that a changing magnetic flux through a circuit induces an emf, with direction constrained by Lenz's law.

definitionAnchor.quote: changing magnetic flux induces an emf

facts.text: Induced current direction opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
Changing field strength, area, or orientation can change magnetic flux.

kernels.definition: Inductance measures how a circuit element resists changes in current by inducing emf through changing magnetic flux.

definitionAnchor.quote: self-induced emf opposes the change in current

facts.text: An inductor stores energy in its magnetic field.

anchor.quote: energy stored in the magnetic field

facts.text: A changing current creates a changing magnetic flux that induces back emf.

anchor.quote: Inductance is the property of a device that tells us how effectively it induces an emf in another device

mcItems.q: If the voltage across an ohmic conductor doubles, what happens to the current?
op: The current remains the same
The current is halved
The current doubles
The current triples
mcItems.ex: Current is proportional to voltage for an ohmic device at fixed temperature. The current is halved because current is proportional to voltage.

mcItems.q: Which factor influences the resistance of a material?
op: Only the material composition matters
Only the length of the conductor matters
Material, length, area, and temperature affect resistance
Only the temperature affects resistance
mcItems.ex: Resistance depends on material, length, cross-sectional area, and temperature. Only the temperature affects resistance because resistance depends on material, length, cross-sectional area, and temperature.
